stories.headline: Former NFL star Antonio Brown to accept plea deal, avoid prison
stories.summary: Former NFL star Antonio Brown will accept a plea deal in his second-degree attempted murder case, resulting in probation, his attorney said.
stories.body:
Former NFL star Antonio Brown will accept a plea deal in his second-degree attempted murder case, resulting in probation and avoiding the possibility of a decades-long prison sentence, his attorney said Wednesday.

The deal comes two weeks after Brown's accuser -- the sole alleged victim in the case -- announced that he would no longer participate in Brown's prosecution.

"They made [Brown] an offer he couldn't refuse," Brown's attorney, Mark Eiglarsh, said in a statement. "There is a profound difference between believing you can win a case and deciding that you and your family cannot afford to spend another year, or potentially several years, wearing an ankle monitor and fighting it."

Brown will appear before a judge in one week to formally accept the deal, which will be a reduced charge of aggravated assault, Eiglarsh told ESPN on Wednesday.

"There's no prison, there's no jail, there's no house arrest. There's only straight probation," Eiglarsh told ESPN. "And no alcohol or drug evaluation, no psychological evaluation, no letter of apology, no community service hours, no fines. Just stay away from the victim.

"No one in their right mind will continue with litigation and/or uncertain stand your ground and trial when [the prosecutors] threw that on the table."

Brown, 38, faced up to 30 years in prison if convicted, with a mandatory minimum of 20 years under Florida law, for an incident involving gunfire outside an amateur boxing match in Miami's Little Haiti neighborhood in May 2025. He pleaded not guilty in November 2025 and filed a motion to dismiss the following month based on Florida's "stand your ground" law.

Eiglarsh added that Brown's decision to accept the deal "should not be interpreted as a retreat from his position that he acted lawfully."

The alleged victim, Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu, said through his attorney on Sept. 9 that "he does not wish to participate" in Brown's prosecution. Attorney Richard L. Cooper said earlier this month that Nantambu forgave Brown for the May 2025 incident.

"We believe that the ends of justice are accomplished with this plea deal, and my client wishes Mr. Brown good health," Cooper told ESPN on Wednesday.

After the May 2025 incident, Brown spent nearly six months in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, where he traveled after the incident, before being extradited by U.S. marshals. Brown was released on $25,000 bail and placed on house arrest with a GPS ankle monitor.

According to the "stand your ground" motion, Brown was trying to get to his car for safety after Nantambu had attacked him. Police said Brown punched Nantambu in the face and, along with two others, continued the attack.

Nantambu walked away, according to a police description of the security footage. Brown then "chases him down with a gun and shoots at him at point blank range," according to a prosecutor. Police added that video from social media showed Brown with a gun in his hand near Nantambu. Two gunshots followed. Nantambu ducked after the first shot was heard, police said.

The stand your ground motion, which acknowledged Brown as the shooter, indicated he "reasonably feared" that Nantambu was armed and that Nantambu made an "aggressive movement" toward Brown.

"In that moment, Brown again reasonably feared death or great bodily harm," the motion read.

Brown then fired two "warning shots, intentionally aiming away from Nantambu to ensure he would not be struck," the motion asserted. Brown also said Nantambu took the weapon after a struggle and left with it.

Brown, who spent 12 years in the NFL, was an All-Pro wide receiver who last played in 2021 for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers but spent most of his career with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

stories.headline: Inside the basketball of 'One Tree Hill' 23 years later
stories.summary: In honor of 23 years since "One Tree Hill" premiered, James Lafferty & Co. take us inside the basketball heart of the cult classic TV show.
stories.body:
WILMINGTON, N.C. -- "Are you here for the big game?" my new friend behind the car rental counter asked shortly after I touched down in Michael Jordan's hometown.

"People are saying you need to be in line by 7 a.m. if you want a chance at a decent seat," she exclaimed before I could answer.

To my surprise, my big game and her big game were one and the same: the "Hey 23" basketball game celebrating 23 years since the hit television show "One Tree Hill" first aired.

Pausing to look around Wilmington International Airport, it appeared nearly everyone arriving in town had the same purpose. Couples, families and groups of friends of all ages -- all donning black, white and royal blue, and not of the Duke Blue Devils variety.

I had counted at least seven combined "Scott" jerseys and two red Quentin Fields-inspired capes before a handmade "You can't kill Dan Scott" sign diverted my attention.

Then the same cheerful voice snapped me back into focus.

"Your car is ready. Just head to spot No. 23! See you tomorrow!"

Unclear whether my rental assignment was intentional or an omen, I grabbed the keys and stepped out into the North Carolina heat.

If a 23rd anniversary feels arbitrary, you're clearly not a "One Tree Hill" fan.

OTH's premise centered around a pair of half-brothers, Lucas (played by Chad Michael Murray) and Nathan Scott (played by James Lafferty) who starred on their high school basketball team in the fictional North Carolina small town of Tree Hill.

The beloved teen drama -- and in my entirely unbiased opinion, the most slept-on basketball show of our generation -- followed Nathan Scott, aka No. 23 and his journey from winning a state championship in high school to being recruited by Duke until his college plans were derailed by his involvement in a point-shaving scheme. Scott eventually went on to win a national title at Maryland before suffering a spinal injury the night before the NBA draft. He then mounted a comeback that started with SlamBall, then saw him play in the D-League and finally become the starting point guard for the then-Charlotte Bobcats.

In the 2000s, Nathan's evolution from a brash high school standout to a selfless NBA star left an indelible mark on a generation of fans. The Ravens never existed -- there was no Tree Hill High and no state championship banner. But for the people who watched the scripted show and the actors who portrayed the characters, the basketball was real. In the years since its historic nine-season run from 2003 to '12, it has amassed a cult following of a magnitude I couldn't quite grasp until setting foot where the show was filmed.

'Hey 23'

On Sept. 19, in front of nearly 5,000 fans at UNC Wilmington's Trask Coliseum, the show's stars, including Lafferty, Murray, Antwon Tanner, Robbie Jones, Bryan Greenberg and Stephen Colletti took the court together again.

The crowd, which included fans who had come as far as France, Australia and Greenland for a chance to see the Ravens, lost its collective mind when the Scott brothers (41-year-old Lafferty and 45-year-old Murray) took the court donning jerseys with their characters' names on the back.

From the moment I set foot in Trask Coliseum, the line between fiction and reality blurred.

A large team photo hung on the wall near the concessions. Ravens banners and merch adorned the bleachers along with an outsized mock political banner touting "Dan Scott for mayor." A mascot danced alongside a volunteer cheer squad doing stunts and tumbling in official Ravens uniforms who led the crowd in the wave. Musician Tyler Hilton (who played Chris Keller on the show) performed the National Anthem.

By the time the OTH theme song, Gavin DeGraw's 2003 hit "I Don't Want To Be," blared, we had reached Tobacco Road-level hype without the hostility.

The game was part of a larger reunion including cast meet-and-greets, autograph sessions, a Hilton and Greenberg concert and a fashion show, hosted by "Friends with Benefit" charity events, that turned Wilmington back into Tree Hill for the weekend.

Founder and CEO of "Friends with Benefit," Rae Agostino, who appeared as an extra on "One Tree Hill," credits Lafferty's former charity games during the show's run for sparking the idea.

"I always wanted to do something with charity and 'One Tree Hill,' and I put my two loves together and here we are," Agostino told ESPN.

She also shared that proceeds from the event go to St. Jude Children's Research Hospital and other charities of the celebrities' choosing.

While the basketball was, for the most part, rusty -- the energy was electric.

As one of the cheerleaders, Cassie Danforth, told ESPN about the connection between Wilmington and Tree Hill, its fictional counterpart, "It's the same thing. We are Tree Hill."

The basketball of it all

By all accounts, Lafferty could ball.

"James had to be very good. And he was. James is a very good basketball player," said Paul Johansson, who played Nathan and Lucas' father, the infamous villain Dan Scott. "He had a high basketball IQ as well. You know, like [Steve] Nash or some of the other floor leaders. He had that general quality. He was a leader."

Lafferty was a 17-year-old high school senior fresh off being named MVP of the varsity basketball team at Hemet High School in Hemet, California, when he auditioned for the role of Nathan Scott -- a process that included the final two actors in consideration playing a producer one-on-one at an executive's house to make sure they knew their way around the court.

"I didn't think it was going to be, like, a real test like that. I was trying to sort of take it easy. I was playing all the time at that time," Lafferty said. "I was trying to, I don't know, be polite. And he reminded me that it was not time to be polite, I was basically playing for my job."

In true Nathan Scott fashion, Lafferty shut out his opponent and landed the role.

Despite getting to play only one season of varsity hoops after taking his junior year off to act -- Lafferty played the role of Steve Alford in ESPN's 2002 film "A Season on the Brink" about Bob Knight and the 1985-86 Indiana Hoosiers -- Johansson assured that he could have had a career at the collegiate level had OTH not panned out.

In fact, when the pilot got picked up, Lafferty was already in the dorms at Long Beach State.

"I was planning to try to walk on to their basketball team," he told ESPN. "I was going to go for it. There was no way I was not going to go for it."

But he wasn't the only actor in the Tree Hill universe who had game. Antwon Tanner (who played Antwon "Skills" Taylor), Robbie Jones (who played Quentin Fields) and Johansson all came from basketball backgrounds.

If finding someone with the basketball prowess capable of playing Nathan was a tall order, casting the show's primary antagonist, Dan, presented its own challenge. That is until one of the show's producers crossed paths with Johansson.

"When I was playing in the E League, the Entertainment League in Los Angeles, Brian Robbins, who was our executive producer ... I played against him a lot, so he saw me be competitive, you know, tough," said Johansson. "And he saw that in me, and when I auditioned for the part, he immediately made the connection, 'Oh, I played with this guy. He is Dan Scott.'"

Johansson, who had played on international tours for the Canadian National Basketball Team and starred alongside Magic Johnson in a commercial, said his star-studded E League team included high-profile Hollywood stars such as Leonardo DiCaprio, Tobey Maguire, Nick Cassavetes and Kevin Connolly.

While it might have been his basketball style and imposing presence that helped land him the role, it's worth noting that his on-court mentality was also eerily similar to that of his OTH alter ego.

"Well, I think, you know, losing is a choice. I think if you have the will, then you find a way to win. Winners find a way to win."

If that musing sounds familiar, Johanssen is aware.

"That's a very Dan Scott kind of quote," he said, flashing his best Tree Hill mayoral campaign grin before driving his point home. "Your destiny is in your hands. And, you know, if you outwork out hustle, out think everybody else, then you should win." In case I had any remaining doubt over the Johanssen-Dan Scott connection, Tanner squashed it when I asked who the biggest trash-talker was of the cast.

"Paul. He's a sore loser, so he's gonna do whatever he can to win," Tanner told ESPN. "He would trash talk you, try to talk you out of your game. ... He's the guy you want on your team, but you hate to play against."

For every parallel between Paul and Dan, Robbie Jones brought himself to the immortal character of Quentin "Q" Fields, whose untimely death in Season 6 left fans reeling.

Jones played college ball for Cal from 1996 to 2000 before taking his talents to the American Basketball Association and eventually overseas to France, Argentina and Mexico.

But the most pivotal games he played were pickup ones at UCLA.

"I played against or with everybody you can think of," said Jones. "The most memorable day was when me and Russ Westbrook's team was playing against Kobe Bryant. Russ was still in college and he wanted to guard Kobe and I wanted to guard Kobe, and of course, he ended up guarding Kobe."

I couldn't help but opine that Q would have wanted to guard Kobe, too.

While Jones didn't get the chance to test his defensive prowess against the Black Mamba, he did stumble upon a new career path.

After other players introduced him to a commercial agent, he enrolled in acting class. Jones recalls walking out of class one day to take a call from his basketball agent who had an offer for him to play in France.

"I was like, hold on a second. Let me pray," said Jones. "I had the clarity. I was like, 'You know what, this is crazy, but I think I'm done with basketball.' Then I got an audition for 'One Tree Hill' and that was that. I was still playing basketball frequently so I did a couple dunks, hit a couple shots and they were like, 'Come on. You're in. You'll be fine.'"

Fiction meets reality

Athletes-turned-actors was a recurring theme that extended beyond the main characters on OTH.

The show was chock-full of notable athlete cameos from Rick Fox, Tony Gonzalez and Jerry Rice to Emeka Okafor, Metta Sandiford-Artest (then known as Ron Artest) and Jeff Burton.

While Lafferty could have done without Nathan's whole point-shaving storyline (as a Duke fan himself, he wanted his character to fulfill his life-long dream of playing for Coach K), he had no such hang-ups about Fox portraying the role of sinister loan shark, Daunte Jones.

"I'm a Lakers fan. I watched Rick Fox win rings. He was part of an iconic team -- the most iconic team for me," said Lafferty. "So, you know, to be acting with him, it's funny that he played such a villain ... but it was just a dream come true. Just such a great guy and a good actor. He was so good in that role."

As for Tanner, he still remembers his surprise when Rice appeared on set.

"I didn't know he was going to be on the show 'cause I didn't read the script. It's just when I was on set, I was like, wait, what the ... Jerry Rice? Oh. That's Jerry Rice! And then I met him, exchanged numbers. I was like, 'Hey, man, can I hang out with you?'"

And hang out they did. But Tanner wasn't quite prepared for everything that would entail.

"He took me to workout with him one day. But I didn't go the next day because of that workout," said Tanner. "I was like, 'Do you have a game? I don't know what you training for' ... He ran seven miles in the morning, and then he said, 'Yeah, I've got to go work out after.' I was like, 'Yeah, all right, I'm done. I'm going to bed. I've got to film today. This is not it. I'll meet you later, bro.'"

Outside of the gym, Tanner also had the chance to show Rice around Wilmington.

"I took him out. You know, introduced him to a few of my friends that owned the different bars and stuff downtown that we hung at. He's a phenomenal guy, real cool. I still got a football he autographed for me when we were here. I still got it at home because I'm a super big Niners fan. He's one of my favorite football players ever, all time."

Hall of Fame athletes making their way to Wilmington was only one example of how fiction blurred with reality while filming OTH.

When asked about filming his favorite basketball scenes, Lafferty recounted the pinnacle of Nathan's story arc, when he finally made it to the NBA and was introduced in the starting lineup for the then-Charlotte Bobcats in 2009.

"The crowd was into it. I was worried the crowd was gonna maybe boo or something or just be annoyed. But they got into it."

"My mom was there, my brother was there, my friends flew out. As a kid who grew up wanting to be in the NBA, it was the closest I could possibly get without actually achieving that dream. ... It was truly incredible."

Given all of the above, it should come as no surprise that Lafferty went with Grayson Allen of the Charlotte Hornets when asked what his character's current NBA player comparison would be.

In the early seasons, it was tough to deny that Nathan's persona was giving "Duke guy" energy.

"In the beginning, I felt like there was a similarity there," said Lafferty with a laugh. "I would try to carry myself in that character as someone that a Carolina fan would absolutely love to hate."

An homage to His Airness

For the typical sports fan reading this, you might be wondering when I'm going to address the elephant in the room.

Yes, fans boarded international flights to Wilmington to see their favorite No. 23 play. No, it wasn't six-time NBA champion Michael Jordan. Rather, it was an actor -- and basketball purist -- who is incredibly aware of the magnitude of that statement.

"I was terrified," Lafferty recalled of discovering his character would be donning the GOAT's number while filming scenes in Michael J. Jordan Gymnasium at the NBA legend's former high school.

"I was just like everyone else. I grew up wanting to be like Mike. I saved uprick my money all year so I could go to his basketball camp in Santa Barbara," said Lafferty who hails from Southern California.

"I didn't even know the character was going to be wearing the No. 23. So, first of all, I find out we're shooting in Wilmington and I'm like 'that's where Michael Jordan grew up.' Then I find out we're shooting at Laney High School, and I just couldn't believe it. ... But when I got to set and realized that at my first wardrobe fitting, that he was wearing the No. 23, that's when I was like 'woah, what is going on?' You just didn't do that. I don't even think they made a 23 for a high school jersey, you know what I mean? No one I knew would wear the No. 23. So, I was freaked out."

Lafferty credits the creatives for helping him get on board with the bold choice.

"We talked about it, and I remember they made a really good point ... They were like 'This character would do that. You don't know anybody who would do that, but that's who Nathan Scott is.' In that moment the character clicked for me even more when I realized, OK I understand now. This is the audacity that this kid has. Because in the beginning he was a villain, right? I feel like, looking back on it, what better way to show that this kid needs to be dealt with than that choice."

No one I talked to could say with certainty whether Jordan was aware of the show. But Johansson shared Lafferty's sentiment of what an honor it was to play on such hallowed ground.

"He is the greatest basketball player that has ever lived," Johansson said. "And, you know, I hope that in some way, I believe, he's seen the show and smiles knowing that there's this sort of homage to him. I hope he does."

Ravens brotherhood

The Laney High School connection didn't stop with MJ. One of the actors who portrayed a member of the Tree Hill Ravens basketball team, Jabbar Dickerson, is No. 2 on Laney's all-time scoring list to this day, with 1,365 career points.

Dickerson, whose two brothers are also in the top 5 on Laney's scoring list (for reference, MJ is No. 6 with 1,165 career points) was playing in the high-profile "Battle of the Weekend Warriors" tournament when he got discovered.

As Dickerson tells it, "two guys sitting in the front row asked me if I'd like to do this for a living. They said they were bringing a show here to Wilmington about basketball, and that I had the look and the skill level for it. Honestly, I thought it was two guys jiving with me."

Speaking with Dickerson, it was immediately clear that he's a team-first guy. He was much more comfortable raving about the Ravens brotherhood than recounting his personal accolades.

"You all don't have a clue about the bond and the brotherhood. This team was not just a team. ... When they said cut, every single day, the word was already out about what we were going to do after we left work. Where we were going. What we were doing together tomorrow. You don't get that too often. And not just four or five guys, everybody. That's not even heard of on certain real teams," Dickerson told ESPN. "There's nothing that each and every one of us won't do for each other."

Lafferty and Tanner echoed Dickerson's passion for the game -- and his appreciation for the group of guys who played the Ravens.

"The guys on the team, they really took me under their wing," said Lafferty. "They could see how much I love the sport, and we would just stay in the gym for the first four years of shooting this show. If we were not on set, we were in the gym.

"We were all just militant about making sure that the basketball looked as believable as possible, because we were all basketball players, right? So we had long choreographed sessions where we choreographed all the plays, and then after that was done, we'd scrimmage for hours. So it was a daily thing. ... That part of it didn't feel like a job."

Tanner seconded, "After work we would play for hours. We would go to the rec over at UNCW every day... and we'd scrimmage against the team that played there."

Old habits appear to die hard ,as he even predicted the former Ravens would get some games in between events during the reunion weekend. "Oh, we're going," Tanner said. "I brought my ball and all of my stuff. They're planning it right now."

There's only one Tree Hill

Just like the bond between the cast, the fandom for the show has ceased to wane. If anything, it seems to grow larger as the years go on thanks in large part to streaming.

My repeated attempts to uncover why the show has so much staying power 23 years after it first aired were met with a general consensus by the actors that no one could have seen this coming.

But my post-Wilmington trip hypothesis hinges on the city of Wilmington itself and the cast's relationship to it. It cannot be overstated how big of a role Wilmington plays in keeping the show alive -- and how big a role it played in the cast members' lives while filming.

"It's like a family. We shared a lot of life. Birthdays, kids' birthdays ... you know, just stuff that went on with everybody here. We definitely were part of the community out here," said Tanner of his time in NC.

"To me, it's a second home, you know?" said Lafferty. "And I can see what it is for the fans that come here ... now that I'm a little bit more removed from the show, I can land in Wilmington, I can drive around, I can see what they see. I can see that as soon as you land in this town, you feel like you're in Tree Hill."

It's no wonder that in a place where numerous hit shows and films such as "Dawson's Creek," "A Walk to Remember," "Iron Man 3," and, most recently, "The Summer I Turned Pretty" were filmed, "One Tree Hill" still appears to be a favorite child.

But as for why basketball worked as the vehicle for this coming of age story?

"I think it worked not so much because of the basketball, but because of the way the basketball was a tool to tell the story of these two boys fighting for their own identities with a very powerful father who was the basketball star of that school in his youth ... So they're trying to fight to free themselves from his shadow," said Johansson.

Lafferty's answer is much more romantic.

"I know how I feel about basketball. I know what it did to me. You see that in the show, because it did that to all these guys here too, you know? There's a movie called 'Love and Basketball' and I think there is a special love and a special passion, an intimacy to basketball for people who play it, it's extraordinary what they feel for it, and I think that comes through in the story. I really do."

stories.headline: Bounce-back picks: The fantasy hockey stars looking to turn back the clock
stories.summary: Here are the fantasy hockey players poised to return to past success, and others you should be wary of.
stories.body:
Even Connor McDavid has a down year in him.

In 2024-25, the best player alive slipped from 3.21 fantasy points per game (FPPG) the year prior to 2.60, the kind of "collapse" that would be a career year for almost anyone else. Then he did what the genuinely elite tend to do after a dip: climbed right back to 3.21. If it can happen to McDavid, it can happen to whichever name on your roster you spent last spring apologizing for.

That's the whole bounceback game; separating the skaters who are actually declining from the ones who just caught a bad hand of variance, injuries or linemate roulette, and are now sitting a round or two cheaper than they should be because of it.

Going back to 2009-10, 59 forwards clearing a career mark of 1.7 FPPG have suffered a real down season -- a drop of 0.35 FPPG or more -- and later climbed back above their career average, a feat they pulled off 78 times between them. Some made a career of it: Evgeni Malkin bounced back four separate times, Matt Duchene an almost comical five. The blue line tells the same story, just rarer -- 20 defenders have done it off that same 1.7 bar, with Kris Letang, Roman Josi, Ryan Pulock and Shayne Gostisbehere each rebounding twice. Fewer names, which is exactly why a bouncing-back defender is worth chasing: the position is thin enough that buying one back at a discount can swing your whole season.

And you don't need the archives for proof. Last season alone, Jason Robertson, Mikko Rantanen, Mika Zibanejad and Zach Hyman shook off ugly 2024-25 campaigns up front, while Charlie McAvoy, Adam Fox, Noah Dobson and Brock Faber did the exact same on the back end. Every one of them rewarded whoever drafted them at a discount.

Not every name below carries that 1.7 pedigree, a few are cheaper bets where a bad year has buried a genuinely useful player, but the shape is identical. Down season, recovery profile, discount at the table. Because this is about fantasy value, period, not star power.

So don't overthink the down year. Below are the forwards and defense primed for a possible return to value with a verdict on whether I think the dip is an opportunity or an obituary.

More: Sign up for free | Rankings | Projections | League types

Bounce-back forwards

Auston Matthews, C, Toronto Maple Leafs (29.0 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 2.89/2.98/2.56): The offense stalled without Mitch Marner. Starved of setups, Matthews opened with just 15 goals in the first three months, ranking a very un-Matthews-like 38th in the league. He later endured a stretch of 12 games with no goals before finally scoring in the same game that Radko Gudas ended his season early. The end result was a season capped at 60 games (27 goals, 53 points). But the finish still plays -- he was sixth in the league in shots per minute -- and if Gavin McKenna even partly fills the Marner void, the setups return and the knee is the only thing that has to heal.

Verdict: A clean yes. Matthews is a Rocket Richard-threat at a discount because of a lost year. Just confirm the knee checks out at camp. If it does, don't let him slip out of the first round.

Mitch Marner, RW, Vegas Golden Knights (29.3 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 2.20/2.33/1.96): Year 1 in Vegas was a soft landing, not a letdown, as he drove a line all season and then led the entire NHL in playoff scoring once it counted. He settles in beside William Karlsson on the second line and onto a dangerous power play that has minutes to spare now that Pavel Dorofeyev is gone. Losing Dorofeyev's finishing touch is a concern, not a dealbreaker. Marner will find a new muse.

Verdict: The question is whether he'll be good or trend back toward great. Luckily, the floor on Marner is still a top-50 forward, so it's not as if there is much downside to banking on a bigger season.

J.T. Miller, C/LW, New York Rangers (33.5 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.92/2.23/1.82): His first full season back in New York was swallowed by injuries and a team-wide scoring drought, but he found his game in the second half and posted fantasy relevant totals in March and April. With Vincent Trocheck traded to Utah, Miller is finally locked into the full-time center role he prefers behind Mika Zibanejad instead of shuffling to the wing.

Verdict: Role clarity plus health makes him a strong middle-rounds target. He's 33, so don't chase the peak, but 70-plus points is very much on the table.

Brayden Point, C/RW, Tampa Bay Lightning (30.5 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 2.08/2.38/1.57): The bet here is murkier than it looks. Point missed 19 games and his counting stats cratered -- 18 goals, a career-low 14.0 shooting percentage -- but he waved off injuries as the cause at season's end, saying instead that his game has to evolve as he ages. That's honest, and a little worrying: a healthy-but-declining 30-year-old is a different draft proposition than a hurt one bouncing back. Counterpoint, he's still centering Nikita Kucherov and Jake Guentzel on a top power play, so the setups and volume are there if the finish returns.

Verdict: A calculated gamble, not a slam-dunk yes. The talent and linemates argue for a rebound, as his own words argue caution. Fine as a mid-round dart if he slips - but don't pay for the 40-goal ceiling on faith.

Jesper Bratt, RW, New Jersey Devils (28.1 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.70/2.18/1.73): He didn't decline so much as shed 14 points of power-play production and some of Jack Hughes' availability, though the even-strength chemistry with Hughes never went anywhere. With Hughes healthy, the scoring should climb. The wrinkle is the power play: New Jersey added top-six wing depth this offseason without subtracting any, so Bratt's man-advantage looks aren't the lock they were. He has to earn the PP1 time that drove his best years, not inherit it.

Verdict: A rebound bet with a catch. Healthy Hughes lifts his even-strength floor, but the crowded forward group puts his power-play ceiling in play, and the PP is where his upside lives.

ESPN Fantasy Hockey is the fun, free way to get inside the game. Draft your players, set your lineups and earn points when the pros do. Sign up today!

Nazem Kadri, C/LW, Colorado Avalanche (35.9 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.70/1.95/1.52): The down year was a slog on a bad Calgary team plus a deadline move, and the Colorado reunion hands him far better company to keep. The catch is the depth chart: he projects behind Nathan MacKinnon and Brock Nelson at center, so his ceiling hinges on top-six looks and power-play time.

Verdict: The environment upgrade is real, but temper it. Take him as a mid-round multi-category center, not a star. If coach Jared Bednar commits him to a scoring role, the 20-goal, 60-point version is back.

Tomas Hertl, C, Vegas Golden Knights (32.8 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.80/2.19/1.81): He slid back to about his career rate, and the real drag is depth-chart gravity. In Vegas's loaded top nine, he's the third-line center behind Jack Eichel and William Karlsson. What rescues his value is the power play, where he's locked onto the top unit.

Verdict: A quietly reliable rebound driven almost entirely by PP1. He won't win your league, but he'll out-earn his cost; grab him once the top center tiers clear.

Dylan Strome, C, Washington Capitals (29.5 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.64/2.10/1.62): He's still Washington's top-line pivot, but everything cooled at once last year. Those are classic bounce-back signals, and the Capitals added Jordan Kyrou and Alex Tuch to deepen the scoring around him, and they might even end up flanking him full-time.

Verdict: A textbook draft-low: same premium role, colder-than-real results. Target him in the middle rounds and expect a return to the 70-point neighborhood.

Jordan Kyrou, RW, Washington Capitals (28.3 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.69/1.97/1.44): A trade to Washington is a fresh start after his shooting percentage bottomed out, but the shot volume never did. He ranked 31st in the league in shots per 60 last season, right in the mix with names like Kirill Kaprizov and Kyle Connor, so the finishing slump reads as variance, not decline. He arrives a three-time 30-goal scorer built for sheltered, offensive-zone minutes, whether he lines up with Pierre-Luc Dubois or slots up alongside Strome.

Verdict: Believe the goal rebound with one caveat -- the top power-play spot is a rotation, so his special-teams points aren't locked. A mid-round price for a run back at 30 goals is worth it.

Valeri Nichushkin, RW, Columbus Blue Jackets (31.5 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.42/2.02/1.44): He lands in Columbus off a down year, and the draw is real: he ranked 28th in the NHL in goals per game over the four seasons prior to falling off. The knocks are real, too, though: he only played 212 of the 328 games in those four years, and Columbus is jammed with middle-six forwards fighting for the same minutes.

Verdict: A boom-or-bust multi-category flier. If he wins a top-six job and stays on the ice, the draft spot is a steal. Take him late and be ready to move on if the role wavers.

John Tavares, C, Toronto Maple Leafs (36.0 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 2.11/2.31/1.84): The production didn't just dip, it fell off his own career pace, from 2.31 the year before to 1.84, his leanest full season in years. But the role that made him useful is intact: he anchors a second line with William Nylander, remains a power-play fixture and still gets his net-front goals. At 36 the age is real, but a half-point below his career rate is steeper than his usage says it should be.

Verdict: A modest bounce-back on role alone - the Nylander line and power-play time argue the 1.84 was low, not the new normal.

Alex Ovechkin, LW/RW, Washington Capitals (41.0 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 2.61/2.60/1.85): Even at 41 he led Washington in goals and didn't miss a game. The collapse was specifically on the power play, where his shooting percentage fell off a cliff (a career-low five power-play goals) while the unit kept generating chances at his usual rate. He still owns a top power-play role, and the Jordan Kyrou and Alex Tuch additions should feed the setups.

Verdict: The volume and PP1 real estate make a goal rebound likely; believe in the shot totals and expect the man-advantage finishing to normalize - just don't expect that 2024-25 magic to return.

Made it this far? Create your own league with your own rules and play against your friends today.

Bounce-back defense

MacKenzie Weegar, D, Utah Mammoth (32.7 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.93/2.51/1.96): His rate dipped thanks to the fantasy void of Calgary and the deeper Utah blue line after he was traded, but he eventually settled in next to Mikhail Sergachev on the top pair and looked the part by the postseason. He's a true multi-category starter, as he finished the past three seasons ranked second or third in the league in fantasy points from hits and blocked shots combined.

Verdict: A solid rebound with one ceiling-cap: Sergachev runs the top power play, so Weegar's points lean even-strength. He can still be a No. 2 defender for fantasy thanks to his elite peripherals.

Shea Theodore, D, Vegas Golden Knights (31.1 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.73/1.91/1.54): His power-play value slipped when Vegas leaned on a five-forward attack most nights. And when they did run a defenseman up top, the job stopped being his alone. After Rasmus Andersson arrived at the deadline, the two split the blue line's power-play minutes almost evenly across the games they both dressed. Theodore led on some nights, Andersson on others, and on a couple even Noah Hanifin topped them both. The PP1 role went from Theodore's to a committee.

Verdict: Don't draft Theodore as a lock for power-play quarterback minutes. He'll get them if Vegas backs off the five-forward look, but he has to hold off a legitimate top-pair talent in Andersson, and last year the split was closer to even than settled.

Colton Parayko, D, St. Louis Blues (33.3 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 1.83/2.34/1.66): His ceiling season was inflated by a shooting percentage twice his career norm, and last year's slide came with back and knee trouble plus a more purely defensive assignment. The peripherals are dependable, like top-pair minutes, penalty-kill time and 160-plus blocks.

Verdict: Expect a multi-category floor, not a goal repeat, because the 16-goal spike isn't the baseline. A late-round blocks-and-shots defender who's far more valuable in banger and category leagues than points-only.

Victor Hedman, D, Tampa Bay Lightning (35.7 years old, FPPG career/2024-25/last season 2.06/2.31/1.51): His down year came with the season ending early when he stepped away from the team for personal reasons, not from any erosion of his game. The complication for 2026-27 is new arrival John Carlson, who projects onto the top unit and could split the power-play quarterback minutes.

Verdict: Let someone else pay for the name. The talent still says rebound if he's back and right, but that's the problem. It's one "if" stacked on two more: he turns 36 this season and Carlson's arrival threatens power-play minutes. Any one of those is manageable; all three at a Hedman price is a pick you don't need to make.

stories.headline: Man United transfer strategy 'financial sustainable' as losses increase - CEO
stories.summary: Manchester United's summer transfer strategy had "financial sustainability in mind," according to CEO Omar Berrada, after reporting a increased financial losses.
stories.body:
Manchester United's summer transfer strategy had "financial sustainability in mind," according to CEO Omar Berrada, after the club reported increased financial losses.

On Wednesday, United posted record full year revenues of £677.6m ($900m) and an operating profit of £22.6m ($30m).

However, the club still reported an overall loss of £43m ($57m), up from £33m ($44m) the previous year.

Borrowing increased by £95m ($126m) to a total of £583m ($773m).

United spent £155m ($206m) midfielders Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba in the transfer window.

Big six rivals Manchester City, Liverpool, Arsenal, Tottenham and Chelsea all spent considerably more with City, Liverpool, Tottenham and Chelsea all spending at least £100m ($133) on one player.

And speaking as the club's fourth quarter and full year financial results were published on Wednesday, Berrada hinted at a need for a prudent approach to transfers.

"While these results confirm that we are on the right trajectory, we will continue to take a disciplined approach to ensure our finances remain sustainable," Berrada said.

"With that financial sustainability in mind, we have strengthened both our men's and women's teams during the summer window and our men's team has seen the return of Champions League football to Old Trafford."

- Carrick quashes notion Manchester United are out of shape

- Mikel Arteta agrees a new long-term contract extension with Arsenal - sources

In the news release which accompanied the results, United said: "the club continues on its journey to improve operational efficiency and financial sustainability."

A United source said "stabilising the business has required, and will continue to require, hard work and financial discipline."

Among the expenditures for the year was £8.2m ($11m) paid to Ruben Amorim and his staff after the Portuguese coach was dismissed in January. United saved around £8.5m ($11.3m) after Amorim accepted the head coach job at AC Milan in the summer.

The club also paid off around £150m ($199m) from a revolving credit facility between March and June.

Meanwhile, United's finances revealed they paid £63.5m ($84m) for land associated with plans to build a new stadium.

Berrada said: "Our other main area of focus is our plan to develop a new 100,000 seater stadium. We have now completed the major milestone of securing the land which will form part of the proposed location of the new stadium."

stories.headline: Alpine's Pierre Gasly warns against 'disturbing' threats after teammate Franco Colapinto incident
stories.summary: Pierre Gasly has hit out at the "disturbing" threats he, his girlfriend and his family received after he held up Argentine teammate Franco Colapinto in the closing stages of the Spanish Grand Prix two weeks ago.
stories.body:
Pierre Gasly has hit out at the "disturbing" threats he, his girlfriend and his family received after he held up Argentine teammate Franco Colapinto in the closing stages of the Spanish Grand Prix two weeks ago.

Late in the Madring contest, Gasly appeared to get in the way of his Alpine teammate before making a pit stop.

The time loss left Colapinto vulnerable to the chasing McLaren of Oscar Piastri, and he complained about Gasly several times on the radio, although he was ultimately able to hold on to seventh position.

Gasly said the abuse crossed a line.

"Personally, I find it a little bit disturbing for our sport," Gasly is reported by The Race as saying during media day for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

"I'm a top athlete, so I know I'm exposed, it's always been the case, but the extent of the threats, attacks, I find completely inappropriate, especially when it reaches out to family members, [my] girlfriend etc. I don't think that should be the case.

"Things were not that way in the past and as a sport we just need to find a way to make it a healthier place because you're exposed, you know you are going to be attacked.

"You can be liked, disliked, it's completely fine, but there is a certain line that should not be crossed just because you're behind a screen and a keyboard, and these lines are crossed too many times."

- Isack Hadjar expects wrist injury to 'still be painful' on Azerbaijan Grand Prix return

- Why is the Azerbaijan Grand Prix on a Saturday, not a Sunday? Baku schedule shift explained

- Haas' Esteban Ocon future in F1 unclear: 'Free agent' for 2027 season

Fan abuse has been a regular story when it comes to incidents involving Colapinto, who has become an Argentine sporting hero since his debut in 2024.

FIA race stewards were bombarded with abuse after Colapinto received a penalty at last month's Dutch Grand Prix, while Alpine have had to condemn death threats aimed at Esteban Ocon after the Chinese Grand Prix and at Yuki Tsunoda after last year's Emilia-Romagna Grand Prix.

Australian driver Jack Doohan, whom Colapinto replaced at Alpine in 2025, had to ask the Argentine's fans to "stop harassing my family" last year.

Doohan later revealed he had "six or seven threatening emails that all my limbs would be cut off" if he was still driving instead of Colapinto at that year's Miami Grand Prix, which prompted police intervention.

It has not just been one-way. Alpine publicly condemned social media abuse aimed at Colapinto in April this year, as well as dismissing the "completely unfounded" suggestion that they were sabotaging the Argentine driver in favour of Gasly.

Speaking on Wednesday, Colapinto stressed that he and Gasly have a good relationship and said he hopes to see the abuse stop in future.

"I think he got a lot of people messaging him," Colapinto said on the subject of Gasly's abuse. "I haven't seen it because I'm not on social media a lot, but it's never nice to get it, even more when it's happening to the team that I'm racing in.

"We are team-mates and we get on very well together. We are playing and focusing on the same result, and [have] the same goal and the same target -- that is to make Alpine better. We are always working as a team and it's not nice to see it.

"So, hopefully, they can stop it. The same happened to other drivers -- Yuki [Tsunoda] last year, it was quite bad as well at one point, I talked about it.

"The stewards, after Zandvoort, I went to see them as well. They had some abuse after the penalty they gave me. It happens a lot with fans in Formula 1, in any sport nowadays, it's something very common.

"Unfortunately, that shouldn't be common. Definitely, we should be taking more care about the things, the words that come out of the keyboards of everyone."

He added: "Hopefully, it doesn't keep happening. But it's something tricky with fans in the sport. It's not just my fans. I've got some very passionate ones. They want me to do well. Hopefully, they can enjoy the good results I'm having."

Sept. 23: Wednesday's news to know

By Todd Zola

Today's action gets underway at 1:10 p.m. ET with an interleague affair in Motown. The Detroit Tigers host the Washington Nationals in a game between clubs playing out the string.

For the second straight day, a pair of teams will be taking the field twice, with the Toronto Blue Jays and Baltimore Orioles making up yesterday's rainout with a separate-admission doubleheader at Camden Yards. The good news is that Mother Nature should cooperate today, with early forecasts favorable everywhere. The bad news is that things could get ugly this weekend, with rain expected in the Northeast.
The Los Angeles Dodgers expect to have Shohei Ohtani serving as their designated hitter when they host the San Diego Padres this evening. Manager Dave Roberts indicated that Ohtani will be examined today and, barring a surprise, will return to the lineup. He's been convalescing on the 10-day IL, taking care of lingering knee and biceps issues.
Ceddanne Rafaela is expected to return to the Boston Red Sox lineup tonight when they host the Cleveland Guardians. The Gold Glove center fielder has been out for over two weeks with a right quad strain. Nate Eaton will return to his reserve role.
Ronald Acuna Jr. had to leave last night's Atlanta Braves game in the third inning after fouling a ball off his left shin. He was able to walk off the field with no assistance, and X-rays were negative, so the club is hopeful that he won't miss much time, if any. Brewer Hicklen finished Acuna's at-bat last night and would be the likely replacement if needed.

Be sure to check out the latest fantasy lineup advice as well as the MLB betting tips for Wednesday.

Sept. 22: Tuesday's news to know

By Todd Zola

Tuesday's schedule gets an early start with a doubleheader in the Bronx between the New York Yankees and Tampa Bay Rays. The opener gets underway at 1:05 p.m. ET, with the nightcap being part of the 15-game evening slate. The AL East combatants both have seven games left, with the Rays six games ahead of the Yankees. Winning just one game assures the Rays of winning the division and the No. 1 seed in the American League.

The Chicago Cubs announced Monday that 3B Alex Bregman will miss the rest of the regular season. He was diagnosed with facial fractures after being hit in the side of his face with a foul ball while getting loose in the on-deck circle on Saturday. The veteran does not require surgery, so he might still return to help the club in the playoffs. More will be revealed about his status later in the week.
The Baltimore Orioles pulled C Samuel Basallo from last night's game in the seventh inning. He was hit in the mask with a foul ball earlier in the contest, then was hit a few times with foul tips. The rookie has been the club's main backstop for just over a month, but he's batting just .158/.244/.250 over 25 games during that span. Carlos Narvaez will see more action if Basallo remains out.
In the same contest, Toronto Blue Jays outfielder Brett Bateman exited early due to a sore right hip. X-rays were negative, leaving his status as day-to-day. The 24-year-old outfielder is hitting a surprising .322/.393/.416, though with only two homers and three steals over 37 games. The Blue Jays were already playing without Vladimir Guerrero Jr. thanks to lower-back tightness. He is also day-to-day, with Sean Keys filling in at first base.
The Detroit Tigers placed Colt Keith on the 10-day IL yesterday, ending his season. The infielder's .258/.322/.406 final line mirrors last year's effort, with a tad less power but a few more stolen bases.
Reinforcements are returning for the Los Angeles Dodgers, with Andy Pages and Roki Sasaki both set to be activated before tonight's home date with the San Diego Padres. Pages is expected to be reinserted as the regular center fielder, shifting Tommy Edman to the keystone. Pages was out for over a month following surgery on a broken bone in his left hand. Before the injury, he was on pace for his best-ever season statistically. Sasaki missed almost a month due to a blister. He's slated to work out of the bullpen tonight, though his pitch count will be limited.

Be sure to check out the latest fantasy lineup advice as well as the MLB betting tips for Tuesday.

Sept. 21: Monday's news to know

By Todd Zola

The final Monday of the regular season features only three games -- all evening games -- beginning at 6:35 p.m. ET with the Toronto Blue Jays visiting the Baltimore Orioles. A few minutes later, the Detroit Tigers host the Washington Nationals. The San Francisco Giants entertain the Minnesota Twins, closing out the truncated slate, at 9:45 p.m. ET.

Three teams have clinched a postseason berth in the American League -- all from the East. The Tampa Bay Rays are on the cusp of securing the division, with the New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox ticketed to run back their 2025 wild-card matchup in the Bronx.
The Cleveland Guardians lead the Chicago White Sox by one game in the AL Central. The second-place finisher would be in the driver's seat for the final wild card. In the West, the Texas Rangers are one game up on the Houston Astros. The second-place finisher still has an outside chance at the last wild-card spot.
All three National League divisions have been clinched, with the Atlanta Braves ruling the East, the Milwaukee Brewers sitting atop the Central, and the Los Angeles Dodgers having nailed down the West. The Brewers have a two-game lead over the Dodgers for the best record in the Senior Circuit. The seedings for the Wild Card Series could go down to the end, with the Philadelphia Phillies just one game behind the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres. The Arizona Diamondbacks have not yet been eliminated, but they're four games behind the Phillies and a lot has to happen for them to extend their season.
The Blue Jays are set to activate Trey Yesavage from the 15-day IL to start tonight's road game against the Orioles, but they're aiming for only 45-60 pitches from the 23-year-old right-hander. He has been sidelined following meniscus surgery on his right knee and made only one rehab start, recording just two outs in that effort.
River Ryan is poised to make his first MLB appearance since 2024. He was acquired by the Tigers in the Tarik Skubal deal. The 28-year-old right-hander was shelved by a hamstring injury at the time but recently made two rehab starts for Triple-A Toledo. He'll handle a few innings before tagging in Keider Montero as the primary pitcher.
The Nationals will counter with DJ Herz, who has been recovering from April 2025 Tommy John surgery. The 25-year-old lefty threw 20 2/3 innings in rehab, the last 13 with Triple-A Rochester. He worked up to 65 pitches, so Herz could manage at least five frames if he's sharp.
Bryce Eldridge of the Giants has not been placed on the 7-day IL, but he nevertheless remains in the league's concussion protocol. The rookie is unlikely to play tonight against the Twins.

stories.headline: Lions make call on Neale Grand Final ban appeal
stories.summary: Brisbane will head to the AFL appeals board in a desperate bid to free suspended star Lachie Neale for the grand final.
stories.body:
Lachie Neale has faced a monster media pack on arrival in Melbourne as the star Brisbane midfielder appeals his suspension for the AFL grand final.

Neale remains banned for Saturday's premiership decider against Fremantle after failing to argue his way out of a one-match suspension for a gut punch on Hawthorn's Jack Ginnivan.

The dual Brownlow medallist gave a short statement after arriving at Melbourne Airport with Lions teammates on Wednesday.

"Very hopeful that it's successful, but regardless of the result, I'll be here to support the boys and the club," Neale said.

"It's a big week for the club."

Following the 15-second statement, Neale was chased by cameras as he immediately left the Virgin Australia terminal.

Fellow Lions veteran Dayne Zorko conducted a press conference after Neale's departure, with the majority of questions focused on the dual premiership co-captain.

Neale was also the story of grand final week last year, famously overcoming a calf injury to play a second-half cameo in Brisbane's demolition of Geelong.

"Lots of scrutiny last year about whether he'd play, whether he wouldn't," Zorko said.

"(20)24 he had a broken foot, so we're used to it.

"It's a lot (the attention), but he seems to be fine.

"I sat next to him on the plane.

"He's just taking it in his stride."

To succeed at an appeals board hearing on Thursday at 4pm, Brisbane will have to prove the tribunal finding was either an error of law, an unreasonable decision, a manifestly excessive classification, or a manifestly excessive sanction.

"There's been 10 (gut punch) incidents this year, all of them have resulted in a week (suspension)," the AFL's footy boss Greg Swann told reporters on Wednesday.

"That was the third (tribunal) appeal and they've all been upheld."

At the end of a four-and-a-half hour hearing on Tuesday night, the tribunal decided not to enact the 'exceptional and compelling clause' to allow Neale to avoid suspension.

Why? For many reasons, according to tribunal chair Jeff Gleeson KC.

There was Neale's evidence, which Gleeson rejected as "inconsistent".

Neale insisted he didn't strike Ginnivan during last Saturday night's preliminary final.

"We have listened carefully to Mr Neale's evidence but we find it was inconsistent in key respects with what we saw on the video," Gleeson said.

Neale maintained his shoulder and chest made contact with Ginnivan; the tribunal found it was "a forceful blow delivered with a swinging arm and an open hand".

That's the guilty part. Next was what Gleeson described as "the more difficult issue".

Was using the exceptional and compelling circumstances clause justified to downgrade Neale's penalty from a ban to a fine?

Introduced this year, the clause had been deployed once: to downgrade a one-game ban to Collingwood legend and the AFL's games record holder Scott Pendlebury, to a fine.

But Gleeson noted Pendlebury was charged with rough conduct. Specifically, graded as careless conduct, medium impact, and high contact.

Neale was charged with striking graded as intentional conduct, medium impact and body contact.

Then, there was Neale's record, which his barrister - the AFL's former football operations boss, Adrian Anderson - compared to Pendlebury.

Until Tuesday night, Neale had never been banned in a 15-year career including two Brownlow medals, six club champion awards, and captaining the Lions to two premierships.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Union skyrocket as unbeaten streak reaches 11 games
stories.summary: Can anyone stop the Philadelphia Union? Their latest win powered them up the charts in this week's edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

In one of the most important matches of their end-of-season schedule, Sam Surridge scored in the fourth and 91st minutes to help secure a 2-2 draw against Miami. With the point, Nashville is winless in three (two draws, one defeat) but still in a position to break Inter's Supporters' Shield record with nine games to go.

2. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 2

Nashville further tightened their grip on the Supporters' Shield with a 3-0 win over Chicago on Saturday. A dominant first-half display mixed with some savvy transition attacking in the second half saw all three of the club's designated players find the back of the net.

3. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 3

The Whitecaps took care of business against Salt Lake by a 3-0 scoreline, thoroughly outplaying their hosts. Few teams in the league can match Vancouver for attacking difference-makers, with summer signing Yadaly Diaby making his first league start and notching two goal contributions.

4. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 4

Inching closer to full health, star left back Sergio Reguilón saw the field in the second half as Miami played to a 2-2 draw with San Diego. While the attack still lacks balance without a threat coming down the wings, even a partially hampered Inter Miami squad still boasts some of the sport's best-ever attackers. Lionel Messi and Luis Suárez both found the back of the net Sunday.

5. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 8

Riding the high of his first call-up to the U.S. men's national team, Peyton Miller bagged a brace in the Revolution's 4-2 victory over Orlando on Saturday. With his sizzling speed and developing goal threat, the 18-year-old did well to help lead New England in the absence of the injured Jack Harrison.

6. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 13

Can anyone stop the Union? Despite falling into a three-goal hole on the road in Kansas City, Philadelphia scored four goals in a nine-minute span in the second half to claim a 4-3 win. They've now gone 11 straight games without a loss in league play.

7. LAFC
Previous ranking: 6

Despite taking a 2-0 lead over San Jose in the California Clásico, a 10-man LAFC couldn't hold on for all three points against their in-state rivals. Two second-half concessions, including one late in stoppage time, turned three points into one in a 2-2 draw.

8. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 11

Allan Saint-Maximin opened his Charlotte account with a goal in a 2-1 victory over D.C. United on Saturday. If coach Dean Smith can tap into the former Newcastle man's one-on-one dribbling and his goal threat, Charlotte FC will be a difficult postseason out.

9. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 10

For more than 45 minutes of action, it looked as if Mateusz Bogusz's penalty conversion had sealed a win for the Dynamo over Cincinnati. However, late in second-half stoppage time, the Polish attacker conceded a penalty that allowed the visitors to equalize at 2-2.

10. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 12

Missing Antoine Griezmann because of a thigh injury suffered in their midweek U.S. Open Cup semifinal defeat, Orlando fell 4-2 to New England. Outside of Lionel Messi, there might not be a player more important to his team's trophy chances than the Frenchman.

11. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 9

A 3-0 loss to Nashville marked seven straight games across all competitions for the Fire without a win. While Robert Lewandowski's scoring record has been positive since he arrived in MLS, it looks as if Chicago's major shift up top has destabilized so much of what propelled them in the spring.

12. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 7

Life has been a slog for New York City lately. A series of poor results over the past two months was extended to include a 1-0 defeat Friday at the hands of their biggest rivals: Red Bull New York. While they created enough chances to win, conversion in front of goal lagged for NYCFC.

13. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 5

Cincinnati left it late but managed to earn a 2-2 road draw against the Dynamo. Kévin Denkey's penalty in the 97th minute rescued the trip, though that doesn't change the fact that Pat Noonan's team has gone five games without a victory.

14. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

After three consecutive victories before this weekend, Dallas played Austin to a 0-0 draw Saturday. Though they created the better chances, Brad Stuver's impressive goalkeeping limited the home side to a solitary point.

15. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 17

It was hardly a dominant showing from the Galaxy, but Greg Vanney's team managed a comeback 3-2 victory on the road in Minnesota, with a makeshift front line that featured Chucky Lozano playing underneath the striker and fullback Harbor Miller back in the attack. Still, all three points count the same.

16. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 16

Thanks to a brace from Anders Dreyer, San Diego earned a 2-2 draw with Miami on Sunday night. While the sophomore outfit still sits below the playoff line out West, they only trail the ninth-placed Portland Timbers by a single point.

17. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 21

Though their summer slide saw San Jose tumble down these rankings, things have stabilized for the Quakes. Their 2-2 draw with LAFC on Saturday marked five straight results, and Timo Werner's return from injury made the outing all the brighter.

18. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 15

Salt Lake were never truly in their match against Vancouver, allowing two goals in the first 30 minutes and failing to ever mount a convincing attack. With Diego Luna now expected to miss the rest of the season with a knee injury, RSL's path to contention is murkier than at any prior point in the season.

19. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 20

Between his call-up to the U.S. men's national team and his goal to cap off a 1-0 win for Red Bull New York in the Hudson River derby against New York City, Julian Hall has had quite the week. Along the way, Michael Bradley's team defended well for much of Friday's game, which hasn't always been true of them in 2026.

20. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 22

The Sounders' summer signings helped rescue a 3-3 draw in Colorado, with Dejan Joveljić and Caden Clark each nabbing a goal to see their new outfit equalize in Colorado. For a team that's still dealing with a slew of injuries, every point is crucial.

21. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 25

Don't look now, but Austin have managed seven straight results in league play. Most recently, they held Dallas to a scoreless draw thanks to some impressive goalkeeping and possession control. It's not flashy, but there's momentum building for 2027.

22. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 27

The good? New winger Morgan Whittaker scored a brace in his first MLS start and looks the part of a superstar. The bad? The Rapids blew a multigoal lead to draw 3-3 at home with Seattle.

23. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 26

Laurent Courtois' return to Montréal went as well as the interim manager could've hoped. His Columbus team dispatched their hosts -- who double as the Frenchman's former employer -- by a 2-0 scoreline.

24. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 18

Minnesota have dropped points from winning or even positions in each of their past five games, including Saturday's 3-2 home loss to the Galaxy. It's safe to say things have gone off the rails for the Loons.

25. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 19

Every now and then, you come up against a team that puts you in your place. That's what happened for Toronto in their 3-1 loss to St. Louis. There's still a distance for Toronto to go before they're on the level of MLS's best.

26. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 24

The Timbers put up a valiant late-game effort and scored in the 93rd minute, but it wasn't enough to salvage a point in Texas as they stumbled to a 2-1 defeat to Dallas.

27. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 23

While they largely outplayed Charlotte, D.C. still fell 2-1. Even when the team plays well, results still aren't trickling into the nation's capital. D.C. United have just six wins this season, one more than bottom-feeders Montréal and Kansas City.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 28

There haven't been as many moments of Aleksei Miranchuk magic as Atlanta would've hoped for when they signed him from Atalanta, but the playmaker delivered Saturday. His goal made the difference in the Five Stripes' 1-0 road win over the Timbers.

29. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 29

What looked destined to be a second straight impressive victory for Kansas City turned into a disaster when the hosts conceded four goals in less than 10 minutes to Philadelphia to lose 4-3 on Saturday. Still, André Luiz dominating in the attack after joining this summer is a silver lining.

30. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

Up against their old head coach, Courtois, Montréal fell 2-0 at home to the Crew. At least they're through to the Canadian Championship final?

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail preliminary finals: Yeo and Leota keen to stay Panthers
stories.summary: Isaah Yeo and Moses Leota are both keens to remain Panthers despite interest elsewhere, while Casey McLean is happy for his departing brother.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into the NRL's preliminary finals weekend.

McLean opens up on replacing Crichton

Casey McLean has revealed the message from Penrith that helped ease the pressure of stepping into the centre position vacated by Stephen Crichton last year.

McLean admitted he initially arrived in first grade feeling as though he had to replace the premiership-winning centre, before being encouraged to forge his own identity.

"I walked in here thinking... I've got to replace Critta," McLean said.

"But coming here, the boys and coach, they're kind of just like, 'There's no shoes to fill. You've got to take the spot and make it your own, kind of play to your strengths.'

"'You wouldn't be here for no reason. You've worked hard... just be yourself.'"

McLean has since established himself as a key member of Penrith's backline as the Panthers continue transitioning into their next generation.

Leota disappointed to miss Warriors showdown

Moses Leota has admitted there was some disappointment in seeing the Warriors' season come to an end, denying Penrith a potential finals meeting with his former front-row partner James Fisher-Harris.

Leota retains strong ties to New Zealand and spent years forming one of the NRL's premier prop combinations alongside Fisher-Harris at Penrith before the Kiwi international's move across the Tasman.

"They had a really great season," Leota said of the Warriors.

"It's very sad, but it is what it is. There's some weapons in that team, right? They'll get back here next year."

McLean relishing Gagai battle

Casey McLean is preparing for another battle with veteran Knights centre Dane Gagai, declaring the 35-year-old is still performing as though he is in his prime.

McLean has previously spent time around Gagai in representative camp and has also faced the Queensland veteran on several occasions at NRL level.

"He's such an amazing guy," McLean said.

"I don't think he lets his age [affect him]... he still looks like he's in his prime.

"He's still running around, he's still doing what he's doing, leaving his mark on the game.

Yeo and Leota's future

Isaah Yeo has confirmed his preference is to remain at Penrith beyond his current contract, and is hoping to sort out his future following the end of the season.

"It always has been [my preference to stay]," Yeo admitted.

"The idea is to stay at Penrith as a one club player."

Moses Leota has also affirmed his love for Penrith, with the hope a deal gets done following the 2026 finals.

"[Remaining at Penrith] is massive to me," he shared.

"I've been here basically my whole life."

Casey McLean backs brother at Bulldogs

Panthers gun Casey McLean admitted while he's "gutted" that his brother Jesse will be leaving Penrith next year, but he's excited to see him flourish at Canterbury.

"Obviously pretty gutted that we won't be on the same team," he told ESPN.

"It'll be a weird feeling at first, but I'm super excited for the opportunity that he'll be given [at the Bulldogs]."

He went on to vouch for Jesse's ability on the field, expecting his older brother to remind fans of his talent.

"He does talk a little s--- on the field," Casey joked.

"But he's just an amazing player - he helped me grow as well.

"He's such an amazing role model, not only for myself, but for a fair few boys here as well."
